During the California Gold Rush the major hub where many people went to work was **San Francisco**.  
San Francisco’s only contiguous neighboring municipality is the city of **San Bruno, California**—they share a land boundary along the eastern shore of San Francisco Bay. Thus, the city that shares a border with the Gold‑rush work hub is **San Bruno**.
